question: Many viewers say computer effects always look fake. Why is their own experience poor evidence for that?
answer: Good effects are never noticed. The only shots a viewer can call fake are the ones that failed; digital skies, set extensions, crowds and removed wires pass as plain photography. Stephen Prince shows most digital work in films is this invisible kind, so the bad examples are a biased sample of the whole.
move: If you only catch the failures, you will think everything fails.
ask: Which skill or tool do I dismiss because I only ever notice it when it goes wrong?
trap: Their eyes adapt to effects and see through them better each year.
source: Prince, Digital Visual Effects in Cinema
reference: Stephen Prince, Digital Visual Effects in Cinema: The Seduction of Reality, Rutgers University Press, 2012
